questions.stem: The polynomial \(P(x)=7x^3+9x^2-5cx\) has factor \(x+c\), where \(c\ne0\). Find \(c\).
questions.hint: If (x+c) is a factor, substitute its zero, \(x=-c\), into (P(x)).

keyPoints.note: The factor theorem says that \(P(-c)=0\).

steps.explain: The zero of the factor (x+c) is \(x=-c\). Apply the factor theorem.
Substitute (-c) into the polynomial and collect terms.

questions.stem: The polynomial \(P(x) = x^4 + 4x^3 - 3x^2 + ax + b\) has remainder \(R(x) = 32x + 44\) when divided by \((x^2 - 2x - 3)\). Find the values of \(a\) and \(b\).
questions.hint: Divide by long division until the remainder has degree 1, then equate it to \(32x+44\) (compare the coefficients of \(x\) and the constants).

steps.explain: Divide the leading terms: \(x^4 \div x^2 = x^2\). Multiply back and subtract.
The remainder must equal \(32x+44\). Equate coefficients.

keyPoints.note: Equate remainder coefficients after long division.

questions.stem: The polynomial \(P(x) = x^3 - 4x^2 - x + 4\) has distinct integer roots. Which of the following is NOT a factor of the polynomial?
questions.hint: If \((x - a)\) is a factor then \(P(a) = 0\). The integer roots divide the constant term 4, so test \(\pm 1, \pm 2, \pm 4\). The factor whose root does NOT give 0 is the answer.

steps.explain: Write each factor as a root: \((x+1)\) → \(x = -1\);  \((x-1)\) → \(x = 1\);  \((x+4)\) → \(x = -4\);  \((x-4)\) → \(x = 4\). By the Factor Theorem, test \(P(\text{root}) = 0\).
So \((x + 4)\) is NOT a factor. (The three integer roots are \(-1,\ 1,\ 4\).)

keyPoints.note: Test integer divisors of the constant term.
Find the root that gives P ≠ 0.

questions.stem: The polynomial \(P(x)=2x^4-16x^3+46x^2-55x+21\) is tangent to the quadratic function \(Q(x)=2x^2-7x+3\) at two distinct points \(A\) and \(B\). The point \(B\) lies on the \(x\)-axis. Find the coordinates of the points \(A\) and \(B\).
questions.hint: Tangent points are where \(P(x)-Q(x)=0\) with a DOUBLE root each. Subtract, factorise as a perfect square, then use \(Q\) to find the y-coordinates.

steps.explain: Tangent at two points means two DOUBLE roots, so the difference is a perfect square: \(2\,(x^2+px+q)^2\). Divide by 2 and match.
y-coordinates from \(Q(x)\): \(Q(1)=2-7+3=-2\) and \(Q(3)=18-21+3=0\) (B on the x-axis ✓).

keyPoints.note: P − Q is a perfect square (double roots).

questions.stem: The polynomial \(P(x)=2x^4-16x^3+46x^2-55x+21\) is tangent to the quadratic function \(Q(x)=2x^2-7x+3\) at two distinct points \(A\) and \(B\). The point \(B\) lies on the \(x\)-axis. Hence, show that the line passing through \(A\) and \(B\) is tangent to \(P(x)\) at the midpoint of \(AB\).
questions.answer: A(1,−2), B(3,0): gradient 1, midpoint (2,−1), line \(y=x-3\). \(P(2)=-1\) and \(P'(2)=1\) so the line touches P at (2,−1) with the same gradient.
questions.hint: Find the line AB and its midpoint M. Show M lies on P and \(P'(x)\) at M equals the gradient of AB.

steps.explain: Using \(A(1,-2)\) and \(B(3,0)\): gradient and equation of \(AB\).
The line \(y=x-3\) passes through \((2,-1)\) on \(P\) with the same gradient 1, so it is tangent to \(P\) there ∎.

keyPoints.note: Show the midpoint is on P and P′ equals the gradient.

questions.stem: The polynomial \(P(x)=x^3-4x^2+tx+10\) has roots \(\alpha,-\alpha\) and \(\beta\). Find the three roots and hence find the value of \(t\).
questions.hint: Use sum of roots for β, product of roots for α², then sum of pairs for t.

steps.explain: Sum of roots \(=-\frac ba=4\). The pair \(\alpha,-\alpha\) cancels.
Sum of products in pairs \(=\frac ca=t\).

keyPoints.note: α and −α cancel in the sum, so β = 4 straight away.

questions.stem: If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are the roots of the equation \(x^2+mx+n=0\), find the roots of \(nx^2-mx+1=0\) in terms of \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\).
questions.hint: Use α + β = −m, αβ = n, then compare sum and product of the new roots.

steps.explain: Sum and product of roots of \(x^2+mx+n=0\).
Guess \(-\frac1\alpha\) and \(-\frac1\beta\): check their sum and product.
The sum must be \(-\frac{\alpha+\beta}{\alpha\beta}\) (= minus the \(x\)-coefficient) and the product \(\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\) — both match. So the roots are \(-\frac1\alpha\) and \(-\frac1\beta\).

keyPoints.note: Write m and n using α and β; the new equation's sum is m/n and product 1/n.

questions.hint: Let α = β + γ; the sum of roots then gives α directly.

steps.explain: Also \(\beta+\gamma=\alpha=\frac32\). So \(\beta,\gamma\) are roots of a quadratic.
Verify each value in the original cubic, then state the ordered roots.

questions.stem:
The cubic equation \(2x^3-x^2+x-1=0\) has roots \(\alpha\), \(\beta\) and \(\gamma\).
Show without finding each individual root that

steps.explain: Use Vieta’s formulas for \(2x^3-x^2+x-1=0\): the sum of roots is \(-b/a\), and the sum of pairwise products is \(c/a\).
Expand the square of the sum and rearrange to isolate the sum of squares.

keyPoints.note: Expand (α + β + γ)² and subtract twice the pair-sum.

parts.hint: Substitute each root into the equation and add.

steps.explain: Each root satisfies the equation, so \(2\alpha^3=\alpha^2-\alpha+1\), and likewise for \(\beta\), \(\gamma\).
Substitute (i) and the sum of roots.

parts.answer: Each root satisfies \(2x^3=x^2-x+1\). Adding for α, β, γ: \(2\sum\alpha^3=\sum\alpha^2-\sum\alpha+3=-\frac34-\frac12+3=\frac74\), so \(\sum\alpha^3=\frac78\).

keyPoints.note: Each root satisfies 2x³ − x² + x − 1 = 0; add the three versions.

Sum of the roots taken two at a time.

questions.stem: The polynomial \(P(x)=4x^3-8kx^2+29x-4k\) has three distinct zeroes, with \(k>0\). It is known that \(k\) is one of the zeroes of the polynomial. Show that the other zeroes of the polynomial are reciprocals of each other.
questions.answer: Product of all zeroes \(=-\dfrac{-4k}{4}=k\); with one zero \(k\) the other two have product \(\dfrac{k}{k}=1\), so they are reciprocals.
questions.hint: Let the zeroes be \(k,\ \alpha,\ \beta\) and use the product of roots \(\alpha\beta\gamma=-\dfrac{d}{a}\).

steps.explain: Product of the zeroes of a cubic: \(-\dfrac{d}{a}\) with \(a=4,\ d=-4k\).

keyPoints.note: Use the product of the zeroes.

questions.stem: The polynomial \(P(x)=4x^3-8kx^2+29x-4k\) has three distinct zeroes, with \(k>0\). It is known that \(k\) is one of the zeroes of the polynomial. Show that \(k\) is equal to the sum of the other zeroes.
questions.answer: Sum of all zeroes \(=\dfrac{8k}{4}=2k\); so the sum of the other two is \(2k-k=k\) ∎.
questions.hint: Use the sum of the zeroes \(-\dfrac{b}{a}\) and subtract the zero \(k\).

steps.explain: So \(k\) equals the sum of the other zeroes ∎.

keyPoints.note: Use the sum of all zeroes = 8k/4.
